messages.author: 52490181456ca7ea
messages.subject: Parallel chains in RStan
parts:
Hey guys, 

I'm running different sets of data on the same model in different chains in parallel, 
this can for example be very useful if you are doing some sort of cross validation on your model.

One way of doing this is for example : 
s1 <- stan_model(model_code = hcode) # compile the model
library(parallel)
sflist <- 
  mclapply(1:36, mc.cores = 36, 
           function(i) sampling(object = s1, data = foo_data[[i]], chains = 1,
                                chain_id = i, iter = 1000, warmup = 350,seed = seed)) 

But if you do it with the mclapply from the parallel package, you can't see the progress bars in Rstudio.
So in the newest version of Stan it is actually possible to run chains in parallel(without the parallel package), but I can't figure out if I can input a list of different data sets to run on in parallel(foo_data[[i]]), without the parallel package.

So can I do this with only the sampling function? And if not, can you show me how you did get the output to be printed in the console of Rstudio so I can implement this? 

Best regards,
Jökull Snæbjarnarson

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Parallel chains in RStan
parts:
On Thursday, September 22, 2016 at 10:37:08 AM UTC-4, Jökull Snæbjarnarson wrote:
So can I do this with only the sampling function? And if not, can you show me how you did get the output to be printed in the console of Rstudio so I can implement this?

I believe the only way that you can easily see the progress in a situation like this is to run R from a shell rather than in RStudio. Even still, the progress may look garbled because 36 processes are writing to the same stream.

Ben

messages.author: 83aa4ea66d984b54
messages.subject: Parallel chains in RStan
parts: I suspect you want to stay in R, but you could do this with CmdStan by diverting the output of each chain to a different text file.  If you look up the CmdStan manual in the section on running a Stan executable you'll see the relevant parallel commands for your operating system. Of course, writing to disk will slow things down. You could do this all with system() inside R.

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Parallel chains in RStan
parts:
We don't want to use different data per chain because
it'll change the posterior and all of our diagnostics
are aimed at trying to reject cases where multiple
chains don't explore the same posterior volume.

- Bob
